s1.syndrome_frame: Acute respiratory failure with mediastinal mass and multiple organ involvement
salient_findings: Dyspnea on exertion and acute worsening of dyspnea
Mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea
Pneumomediastinum, left pneumothorax, and lytic destruction of vertebrae
key_facts: 1-month history of dyspnea on exertion, intermittent dry cough, hyporexia, and unquantified intermittent fever
Acute respiratory failure and pulseless electrical activity arrest
Blood pressure 200/140 mmHg, heart rate 100 bpm, respiratory rate 16 bpm, temperature 36 °C, and oxygen saturation 78% on ventilatory support
Anisocoria (right pupil 5 mm, left 3 mm), jugular venous distension, sinus tachycardia, and bilateral coarse rales
Homogeneous right paratracheal mediastinal mass compressing and displacing the trachea to the left, with adjacent right upper-lobe infiltrates on chest radiography
11 × 8.6 × 9.5 cm lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura on contrast-enhanced CT scan
WBC 13.47 × 10^3/µL (85% neutrophils), hemoglobin 9.9 g/dL, platelets 303 × 10^3/µL
INR 1.39, lactic acid 2.83 mmol/L, C-reactive protein 4.20 mg/dL, LDH 592 U/L
Arterial blood gas revealed pH 7.30, PCO2 44.5 mmHg, PO2 122 mmHg, HCO3 22.3 mmol/L, BE –3.7 mmol/L, and SO2 98%
Received dexamethasone and piperacillin/tazobactam
Video-assisted thoracoscopic biopsy planned to obtain adequate tissue

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass and acute respiratory failure are consistent with lymphoma

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Hodgkin lymphoma, Non-Hodgkin lymphoma can present with a mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Thymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Thymoma is a type of tumor that can arise in the mediastinum and cause respiratory symptoms

shortlist.label: Mediastinal sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Sarcomas can present with a mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms, and are a plausible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: This rare disease can present with a mediastinal mass and respiratory symptoms, and is a plausible diagnosis given the patient's symptoms and the presence of a mediastinal mass

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a large mediastinal mass, acute respiratory failure, and systemic symptoms such as fever and weight loss is consistent with an aggressive lymphoma. The presence of a large, lobulated solid mass arising from the right thoracic operculum/pleura and the patient's young age also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: While possible, Hodgkin lymphoma is less likely given the patient's age and the atypical imaging features.

rejected.label: Thymoma
rejected.why: Thymomas are typically slower-growing and less likely to cause acute respiratory failure.

rejected.label: Mediastinal sarcoma
rejected.why: Sarcomas are rare and would not typically present with such systemic symptoms and laboratory abnormalities.

rejected.label: Lymphomatoid granulomatosis
rejected.why: This condition is rare and typically presents with pulmonary nodules and skin lesions, which are not present in this case.
